industries.name: Scheduled Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks & Cooperative Banks
industries.personas: Head of Legal & Stressed Assets, Zonal NPA Recovery Chief, Authorized Officer (SARFAESI), VP Retail & Credit Card Collections, Managing Director (Urban/District Co-op Bank)
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹25,000 (Credit Card / Mudra / KCC) to ₹50 Cr+ (Corporate CC/OD & Term Loans); SMA-1 (31–60 DPD), SMA-2 (61–90 DPD), Sub-Standard & Doubtful NPAs (>90 DPD)
industries.statutory_hooks: SARFAESI Act 2002 (s.13(2) 60-day notice, s.13(3A) representation reply, s.13(4) symbolic possession, s.14 DM/CMM order); RDB Act 1993 (DRT Original Application >= ₹20 Lakh, e-DRT); Legal Services Authorities Act s.19–20 (Pre-Litigation Lok Adalat); NI Act s.138 & PSS Act s.25; Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act s.84 Arbitration; IBC Part III (Personal Guarantors).
industries.competitor_gap: Enterprise SaaS vendors (Credgenics, Spocto) publish high-level marketing brochures gated behind enterprise demos with zero statutory depth, while legal blogs (iPleaders, LawBhoomi) explain SARFAESI/DRT from a law-student or borrower-defense angle. Zero platforms address the massive sub-₹20 Lakh DRT exclusion gap, cooperative bank s.84 arbitration notices, SMA-2 pre-NPA cure notices, or Lok Adalat bulk docket preparation for bank branches.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Onboard Zonal/Regional Bank Panels via LegalRecovery's 'Representees' & Bulk Notice Dispatch engine (simultaneous Zoho Email + WATI WhatsApp + India Post Speed Post RPAD manifest with BSA s.63 certificate), cutting branch-level pre-litigation notice turnaround from 21 days to <24 hours.

industries.name: NBFCs, Digital Lending Fintechs, HFCs & Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)
industries.personas: Chief Collections Officer, Head of Legal & Litigation, Lending Service Provider (LSP) Ops VP, Gold Loan Auction Compliance Head, HFC/MFI Zonal Recovery Head
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹5,000–₹5 Lakh (BNPL, Fintech Personal & MFI JLG Loans) to ₹25 Lakh–₹10 Cr (LAP, Commercial Vehicle, Supply-Chain & SME Unsecured Loans); Bucket X, 30+, 60+, 90+ DPD
industries.statutory_hooks: Payment & Settlement Systems (PSS) Act 2007 s.25 (e-NACH / ECS / UPI AutoPay dishonour — criminal parity with s.138 NI Act); RBI Responsible Business Conduct & Recovery Agent Directions (8 AM–7 PM contact rule, IIBF certification, zero-harassment audit trail); SARFAESI notification threshold for NBFCs (>= ₹100 Cr asset size & >= ₹20 Lakh loan security); Online Institutional Arbitration (Arbitration Act s.21/s.29B fast-track); RBI Gold Loan Auction Fair Practice Code.
industries.competitor_gap: 95% of SERP results for 'loan app legal notice' or 'Section 25 PSS Act notice' target defaulting borrowers seeking debt-settlement relief (Freed, SettleLoans, SingleDebt). Almost zero authoritative pages guide NBFC/Fintech legal heads on executing compliant bulk Section 25 e-NACH prosecutions, gold-loan pre-auction notices, co-lending FLDG invocation workflows, or mid-market alternatives to expensive 12-month SaaS lock-ins.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Native fit with LegalRecovery's built-in 'loan-recovery' schema (`disbursedAmount`, `disbursementDate`, `asOnDate`, 4-step escalation protocol + inbound borrower reply triage), enabling mid-size NBFCs, HFCs, and fintechs to upload 500–10,000 bounced e-NACH mandates via CSV.

industries.name: Doctors, Multi-Specialty Hospitals, Nursing Homes, Clinics & Diagnostic Chains
industries.personas: Hospital Medical Superintendent, Head of Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Hospital CFO / Legal Cell, Clinic Founder / Surgeon, Diagnostic Chain Finance Controller
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹15,000–₹25 Lakh (Emergency/ICU Post-Discharge Patient Undertakings, IVF/Dental/Cosmetic Packages) to ₹10 Lakh–₹5 Cr+ (Delayed TPA/Insurer Batches, CGHS/ECHS/PM-JAY Arrears, B2B Lab Franchises)
industries.statutory_hooks: Indian Contract Act s.73 (Admission Undertaking & Promissory Note enforcement); Article 21 & High Court mandates prohibiting patient/mortal-remains detention (making civil legal notices the ONLY lawful recovery path); IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (strict cashless settlement timelines & penal interest at Bank Rate + 2% payable by Insurer/TPA to network hospitals); CPC s.80 & Art. 226 Writ Mandamus for undisputed CGHS/ECHS/ESIC empanelment dues; NI Act s.138 for stop-payment discharge cheques.
industries.competitor_gap: Currently on LegalRecovery.in (and across Indian legal-tech SERPs), 100% of hospital content is written for aggrieved patients suing hospitals for overbilling or negligence. Zero competitors address the crisis facing 70,000+ Indian private hospitals and clinics: they are criminally barred from detaining non-paying patients at discharge, suffer 90–180 day arbitrary deductions by TPAs/insurers, and hold crores in unpaid CGHS/corporate credit bills with no specialized legal-recovery partner.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Position LegalRecovery as the 'Article-21 & NMC Compliant Healthcare RCM Legal Desk' — offering standardized Discharge Promissory Note packs + ₹999 post-discharge patient recovery notices + bulk TPA/Corporate/Lab-Franchise demand notices.

industries.statutory_hooks: Order XXXVII CPC Summary Suits on Tax Invoices + Drug Delivery Challans; MSMED Act s.15–18 (for Udyam-registered formulation/CDMO/surgical manufacturers); Income Tax Act s.43B(h) 45-day buyer disallowance notice; NI Act s.138/s.141 on stockist security PDCs; AIOCD/State Druggist Association conciliation + statutory Commercial Court s.12A.

Nobody covers orthopedic/cardiac implant 'cath-lab consignment consumption without billing', hospital biomedical AMC defaults, CDMO third-party batch rejection pretexts, or expired/breakage credit-note disputes.

industries.name: IT Services, SaaS Platforms, Software Development, Cloud & AI Agencies

industries.statutory_hooks: Copyright Act 1957 s.17/s.51 (IP & source-code ownership stays with vendor until full payment if MSA structured properly); Commercial Courts Act s.2(1)(c)(xviii) technology/service agreements & s.12A mediation; MSMED Act s.15–18 for Udyam IT service companies; FEMA 1999 & RBI SOFTEX / EDPMS 9-month export realization rules; Contract Act s.27 exception for anti-poaching / employee conversion fee clauses.

Enterprise IT & SaaS founders face completely different battles: UAT sign-off stonewalling ('infinite bug-fix loop'), multi-year SaaS early-termination breach, cloud hyperscaler consumption pass-through defaults, client poaching deployed developers, and SOFTEX write-off freezes.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Advocate-drafted domestic & cross-border IT MSA breach notices served to corporate General Counsel & CFOs + FEMA/SOFTEX best-effort documentation for AD Banks.

industries.name: Manufacturing, Industrial Machinery, Heavy Engineering & Auto-Ancillary OEMs
industries.personas: Factory Managing Director, Industrial Finance Controller, Tier-1/Tier-2 Auto-Ancillary Promoter, Custom Capital-Goods Sales Head
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹3 Lakh–₹10 Cr+ (Custom Machinery 20% Commissioning Balance, Tooling/Die Amortization, CNC Job-Work Challans, OEM Line-Supply Ledgers)
industries.statutory_hooks: Sale of Goods Act 1930 s.42 (deemed acceptance when buyer retains & runs machinery in production without timely rejection) & s.55–56 (suit for price); MSMED Act s.15–18 + MSME ODR Portal (Micro & Small units); Commercial Courts Act Order XXXVII (vital for Medium Enterprises excluded from MSEFC s.18!); Income Tax Act s.43B(h); Arbitration s.9 against wrongful Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG) encashment.
industries.competitor_gap: Generic MSME articles miss the #1 pain point in Indian manufacturing: buyers run delivered machinery commercially for 6 months and then invent 'efficiency/output shortfall' excuses to withhold the final 10–20% retention, or Tier-1 OEMs slap arbitrary retrospective debit notes and tooling cancellations on Tier-2 suppliers. Plus, almost nobody warns Medium Enterprises that MSMED s.18 excludes them!
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Technical-legal demand notices integrating Sale of Goods Act s.42 'commercial usage = deemed acceptance' doctrine + FY-end Section 43B(h) tax-disallowance CFO notices.

industries.name: Infrastructure, Civil Construction, EPC & Turnkey MEP Contractors
industries.personas: EPC Director, Head of Contracts & Claims, Civil/Structural/MEP/HVAC Contractor, Infrastructure Promoter
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹10 Lakh–₹50 Cr+ (Uncertified Running Account [RA] Bills, Post-DLP Retention Money, Price Escalation & Extra-Item Claims, NHAI/CPWD/PWD/Railways Tender Dues)
industries.statutory_hooks: Arbitration & Conciliation Act 1996 (s.21 Invocation, s.9 Interim Asset Security & Bank Guarantee Injunction, s.11 Appointment, s.29A 12-month Award Mandate, s.36 Execution); CPC s.80 (60-day Govt/PSU Notice); Supreme Court jurisprudence invalidating unfair 'pay-when-paid' back-to-back subcontractor clauses where employer delay is indefinite; Art. 226 Writ jurisdiction for admitted/certified PSU bills.
industries.competitor_gap: Competitors treat construction debt like a simple shop invoice. In reality, construction recovery hinges on Joint Measurement Books (MB), uncertified final bills, Defect Liability Period (DLP) expiry, wrongful Liquidated Damages (LD) set-offs, and protecting Bank Guarantees from retaliatory encashment the moment a contractor demands dues!
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Pre-arbitration claim crystallization & Section 21 notices drafted by AMA Legal Solutions' infrastructure litigation panel, seamlessly bridging from ₹999/retainer notice to Section 9 BG stay & arbitral representation.

industries.name: Real Estate Developers, Builders, Commercial Landlords, REITs & Co-Working Operators
industries.personas: Real Estate Developer CRM/Legal VP, Commercial IT-Park / Mall Asset Head, Co-Working / Managed-Office CFO, Industrial Warehouse Landlord, RWA/Commercial Condo Treasurer
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹2 Lakh–₹5 Cr+ (Homebuyer RERA Milestone Defaults, Commercial Office 3-Year Lock-In Breaches, Mall Revenue-Share & CAM Arrears, Enterprise Co-Working Seat Defaults)
industries.statutory_hooks: RERA 2016 s.19(6) & s.19(7) (statutory duty of allottee to pay milestones + SBI MCLR + 2% interest on default, plus due-process cancellation notice); Transfer of Property Act 1882 s.106 (15-day commercial lease termination) + CPC Order XX Rule 12 Mesne Profits; Commercial Courts Act s.2(1)(c)(vii) (agreements relating to immovable property used exclusively in trade or commerce!); Income Tax Act s.194-I TDS certificate recovery.
industries.competitor_gap: Every real-estate page on LegalRecovery today is buyer-vs-builder or tenant-vs-landlord! Yet developers lose crores when investor-allottees stop paying construction-linked demands (and RERA punishes builders if they cancel units without serving strict cure notices). Similarly, co-working operators and Grade-A commercial landlords have zero specialized SEO resources on enforcing unexpired lock-in rent under Supreme Court mitigation rules.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Bulk RERA Section 19(6) cure-cum-interest demand notices for developer CRM teams + Commercial Court s.2(1)(c)(vii) lock-in & CAM recovery notices for landlords and co-working chains.

industries.name: Logistics, 3PL Warehousing, Freight Forwarders, CHAs & Fleet Operators
industries.personas: 3PL CFO, Fleet Owner / Transport Contractor, Freight Forwarder & Customs House Agent (CHA) Director, Cold-Chain Logistics Promoter
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹50,000–₹2 Cr+ (Primary FTL/PTL Freight Ledgers, Truck Halting/Detention & Container Demurrage, Upfront Customs Duty / Ocean Freight Advances, 3PL Storage Monthly Bills)
industries.statutory_hooks: Carriage by Road Act 2007 + Indian Contract Act s.170–171 (Bailee's / Carrier's Particular Lien vs Contractual General Lien on GR/Bilty); Major Port Authorities / Bills of Lading & Maritime/Air Freight forwarder agency recovery; GST E-Way Bill + Signed POD/Bilty as conclusive proof for Order XXXVII CPC Summary Suits; Warehouseman's lien & auction notice procedure.

industries.lr_funnel_hook: Rapid 48-hour Carrier Lien & Freight Demand Notices (essential while cargo is still in transit/warehouse) + bulk overdue Bilty/POD ledger recovery for 3PL finance teams.

industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹75,000–₹8 Lakh (8.33%–16% Permanent Placement Fees & Backdoor Hires) to ₹5 Lakh–₹3 Cr (Monthly Temp-Staffing Payroll + PF/ESIC Bills, Corporate/Society FMS Contracts)
industries.statutory_hooks: Contract Act s.70 (Quantum Meruit / 'Effective Cause of Introduction' doctrine even where client evades signing candidate-acceptance sheet); Order XXXVII CPC Summary Suits on Terms of Business (ToB) + ATS/Email timestamps; IBC s.8 Operational Debt for large staffing/FMS payroll arrears (>= ₹1 Cr); MSMED Act protection for Udyam-registered staffing & security agencies.
industries.competitor_gap: Recruitment and staffing agencies bleed working capital in two brutal ways: (1) 'Backdoor Hiring'—clients reject a CV on email and secretly hire the same candidate 60 days later; and (2) Temp-staffing & security agencies MUST pay statutory wages, PF, and ESIC by the 7th/15th even when the corporate client withholds invoices for 120 days! Almost zero Indian legal-tech pages provide actionable recovery playbooks for either.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Specialized 'Backdoor Hire Detection & Fee Demand Notice' + urgent 15-day Payroll/PF Arrears Recovery Notices for staffing & security agencies.

industries.name: Textiles, Apparel, Garment Manufacturers, Dyeing Units & Yarn / Spinning Mills
industries.personas: Spinning / Weaving Mill Owner, Garment Exporter / Domestic Manufacturer (Tirupur, Surat, Ludhiana, Noida, Bhiwandi, Kolkata, Ichalkaranji), Dyeing/Processing Job-Worker, Yarn Wholesaler
industries.ticket_and_buckets: ₹1 Lakh–₹2 Cr+ (60–120 Day Grey/Finished Fabric Credit, Broker/*Adatiya*-Mediated Sales, Retail Brand SOR Returns, Buying-House Cancelled Export Orders)
industries.statutory_hooks: MSMED Act s.15–18 & Income Tax Act s.43B(h) (game-changer in Surat/Tirupur textile credit cycles!); Indian Contract Act s.170 Bailee's Particular Lien (for dyeing, bleaching, printing & embroidery job-workers holding processed fabric); Contract Act s.182–238 Agency & *Del Credere* Textile Broker liability; NI Act s.138 on PDCs & Hundis; Textile Panch / Mahajan arbitration awards enforcement.

When buyers abscond ('party uth gayi') or dump unsold seasonal garments back under fake 'colour-bleeding / shrinkage' complaints after 90 days, generic corporate law blogs offer zero practical guidance on binding the textile broker, leveraging Section 43B(h), or enforcing Mahajan arbitration.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Bilingual (English + Hindi) multi-party notices served simultaneously on Buyer + Introducing Textile Broker/Agent + Company Directors via WhatsApp, Email & Speed Post.

industries.statutory_hooks: Sale of Goods Act s.37/s.42 (once RMC is poured into slab or steel is embedded in structure without 48-hour cube/MTC test objection, buyer loses right to reject!); Order XXXVII CPC Summary Suits backed by Weighbridge Slips + GST E-Way Bills + Gate-Entry Stamps; IBC s.8 Operational Creditor Form 3/4 against real-estate/infra corporate debtors (>= ₹1 Cr); NI Act s.138/s.143A.

Zero websites teach material suppliers how to pre-emptively lock delivery acceptance and defeat sham quality defenses.
industries.lr_funnel_hook: Evidentiary Demand Notices annexing E-Way Bill Part-A/B, Weighbridge Slips, Mill Test Certificates (MTC), and Site Gate-Inward stamps to neutralize fake quality disputes before NCLT/Commercial Court.

industries.lr_funnel_hook: Reputation-safe, RTE & CBSE-compliant 'Parent Fee Arrears Civil Legal Notice' batches via LegalRecovery's Representee portal (recovering fees strictly from earning parents without ever penalizing the child or holding TCs!).

industries.lr_funnel_hook: SLA & DPDP-compliant Pre-Suspension Cure Notices + Bulk Enterprise Postpaid / CPE Hardware Recovery batches.
